title: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol is dramatically better at migrating legacy code
description: OpenAI announced that its GPT-6.1 Sol model significantly improves the ability to write and migrate legacy code in older programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages underpin critical infrastructure and essential services globally. The model shows high accuracy in migrating COBOL programs to modern languages without changing behavior, potentially aiding modernization efforts. However, production migrations still require expert review and testing. There is no indication of a security vulnerability or exploit associated with this advancement.
aiSummary: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model demonstrates substantial progress in generating and migrating software written in legacy programming languages, including COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. Using the MultiLangBench benchmark, GPT-6.1 Sol achieved high accuracy rates in building a SQLite-compatible database engine and migrating COBOL code to languages like C++, Java, Kotlin, Python, and Rust. This capability could assist organizations in modernizing legacy systems that support critical infrastructure. The announcement does not describe any security vulnerabilities, exploits, or threats related to this technology.
aiImpact: There is no direct security impact or threat described. The improvements in AI-assisted code migration may facilitate modernization of legacy systems, which could indirectly affect security posture by enabling updates and replacements of older software. No active exploits or vulnerabilities are reported.
